highlights.title: Claude Code v2.1.219: Claude Opus 5 Now Default with 1M Context
highlights.summary: Claude Code v2.1.219 introduces Claude Opus 5 as the new default Opus model, offering a massive 1 million token context window at $10/$50 per million tokens in fast mode. It also adds a `sandbox.network.strictAllowlist` setting that blocks non-allowlisted hosts in sandboxed commands without prompting, improving security. A new `DirectoryAdded` hook also fires after a directory is added, enabling more powerful automation workflows.

highlights.title: Introducing Claude Opus 5 — Anthropic's Most Powerful Model
highlights.summary: Anthropic officially announced Claude Opus 5, now the most capable model in the Claude lineup and the new default for Opus-tier tasks in Claude Code. With a 1 million token context window, it can handle entire codebases or long-running agentic sessions in a single context. Developers using Claude Code will automatically benefit from this upgrade as it becomes the default Opus model.

highlights.title: Claude Code v2.1.218: /code-review Now Runs as a Background Subagent
highlights.summary: The `/code-review` slash command has been redesigned to run as a background subagent, meaning review output no longer clutters your main conversation thread. This also ensures that stacked slash commands correctly use the reviewed code as their target, making multi-step review-and-fix workflows much smoother. Screen-reader accessibility was also improved with announcements for deleted text.

highlights.title: Hardcoded Instruction Tells Opus 5 Not to Use Subagents in Claude Code
highlights.summary: Developers discovered that Claude Code has a hardcoded system prompt instruction preventing Claude Opus 5 from spinning up subagents, which has sparked debate about transparency and control in agentic workflows. This is especially relevant given Anthropic's separate announcement that they removed over 80% of Claude Code's system prompt for Opus 5 and Fable 5. Understanding these hidden constraints can help you better plan tasks where you expect multi-agent behavior.

highlights.title: Claude Code v2.1.216: Fixed Quadratic Slowdown in Long Sessions
highlights.summary: Version 2.1.216 patches a significant performance bug where message normalization costs grew quadratically with the number of conversation turns, causing multi-second stalls in long sessions and slow resumes. A new `sandbox.filesystem.disabled` setting lets you skip filesystem isolation while still keeping network egress controls active. If you've noticed Claude Code getting sluggish in extended coding sessions, updating to this release should help noticeably.

highlights.title: Get EVERYTHING Out of Claude Code in 13 Minutes (Beginner to Pro)
highlights.summary: This YouTube tutorial offers a fast-paced walkthrough of Claude Code from the absolute basics up to more advanced usage patterns, all in under 15 minutes. It's a great starting point for developers who want a practical overview without committing to a multi-hour course. Watch this first before diving into longer resources to get a solid mental model of the tool.

highlights.title: CogniKernel: Cross-Session and Cross-Platform Memory for Claude Code
highlights.summary: CogniKernel is a community-built open-source tool that adds persistent memory to Claude Code, allowing context and knowledge to carry over across different sessions and even different machines. It cloned nearly 600 times within a week of launch, showing strong demand for memory continuity in AI coding workflows. If you find yourself constantly re-explaining your project context to Claude Code, this tool could save significant time.

highlights.title: Claude Code v2.1.217: Emoji Shortcode Autocomplete in Prompt Input
highlights.summary: Version 2.1.217 adds emoji shortcode autocomplete to the Claude Code prompt input — type `:heart:` to insert ❤️ or `:hea` to see suggestions, with the option to disable it via `emojiCompletionEnabled`. It also adds helpful warnings when transcript writes are failing due to issues like a full disk, so you won't silently lose session history. These small quality-of-life improvements make daily usage more reliable and expressive.

tips_of_the_day: After upgrading to Claude Code v2.1.219, explicitly set your model to `claude-opus-5` in your project settings to take advantage of the full 1M token context window — ideal for large monorepos or long refactoring sessions.

Use `/code-review` before running a fix command: since it now runs as a background subagent, you can stack it with a follow-up slash command like `/fix` and Claude Code will automatically apply fixes to the reviewed code without cluttering your main chat.

If your Claude Code sessions feel slow after many turns, make sure you're on v2.1.216 or later — the quadratic message normalization bug fix can dramatically speed up long-running sessions, especially after 50+ conversation turns.
